title: Silverpine Token Econ Playbook — POC scoping
meeting_header: Date: 2025-10-14 | Start: 16:00 PT | Duration: 62m | Platform: Zoom | Recording: available | Attendees: Maya Chen, Rafael Ortiz (Redwood); Priya Nair, Tom Becker, Janelle Park, Evan Liu (Silverpine)
summary: POC scoping focused on unit economics for Silverpine's summarization/ingestion workload. Discussed per-token costing, batching and KV cache knobs, target latency SLOs, benchmark plan (latency and cost), and timeline for a 6-week POC. Silverpine concerned about bursty traffic, sensitive customer data, and budget cap. Redwood proposed a staged benchmark with 3 model configs (base, quantized, cached) and defined success criteria tied to cost per 1M tokens, 95th percentile latency, and accuracy delta on evaluation set.
next_steps: Redwood to send detailed benchmark plan + pricing workbook by 2025-10-17
Silverpine to provide 5 sample prompts and representative traffic histogram by 2025-10-20
Schedule bench kickoff (2 hours) week of 2025-10-27
Follow-up legal: sign mutual NDA (if needed) — Janelle to confirm by 2025-10-18
action_items: Maya Chen: Share pricing workbook and bench template (due: 2025-10-17)
Priya Nair: Drop 5 canonical prompts and a 2-week traffic histogram to the shared folder (due: 2025-10-20)
Rafael Ortiz: Prepare three model/quantization configs and a latency/cost projection (due: 2025-10-16)
Janelle Park: Confirm data residency & KMS requirements and whether Silverpine needs on-prem (due: 2025-10-18)
Tom Becker: Identify internal stakeholder for SLA discussion (due: 2025-10-22)
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this one. we also have Rafael from our SE team and Anita from customer success. 00:07 Priya Nair: hi thanks, Priya here. excited to map this out. quick note, our traffic is pretty spiky due to nightly batched imports plus interactive user queries during business hours. 00:18 Rafael Ortiz: okay, great. that's exactly the kind of thing we need to size for — can you give ballpark qps during peaks and off-peak? 00:27 Priya Nair: sure, peak interactive is 120 qps for short prompts (200–400 tokens), nightly batch ingest hits sustained 4k concurrent streams but each is long—like 4k*10k tokens across the run, but it's spread over 3 hours. the key bit is cost, we have a hard monthly inference budget. 00:46 Tom Becker: and latency SLO is 300ms p95 for interactive requests, otherwise batch can be minutes. 00:54 Rafael Ortiz: okay p95 300ms, good to know. so on the cost side, we'll model per-token inference cost across three configs: full fp16 baseline, int8 quantized, and cached + quantized variant. quick FYI, caching prefixes/KV can drastically drop per-token compute for repeated contexts — but effectiveness depends on prompt overlap. 01:12 Priya Nair: yeah we do have a lot of shared prefixes — like user instructions and many templates. that should help. 01:20 Evan Liu: question: what does Redwood treat as a token for billing — input+output or output only? 01:25 Maya Chen: standard is input + output for hosted usage; for dedicated we can propose different metering, but for the POC we'll model both inclusive and output-only to show sensitivity. 01:35 Janelle Park: security — we need SOC 2 type II, SSO, KMS integration, and logs forwarded to our SIEM — are those in scope for a POC? 01:44 Anita Kapoor: yes, we can enable audit logging for the bench and demo a KMS integration in the Private trial. for hosted we have tenant-level encryption and exportable audit logs. 01:55 Priya Nair: good. now about the benchmark — what metrics do you recommend we run? 02:02 Rafael Ortiz: suggest: cost per 1M tokens (separate for input/output), p50/p95 latency for interactive profile, tokens/sec and GPU utilization for batch profile, and accuracy delta versus your gold eval set (we'll need a small eval). also memory/kv cache hit rate. 02:18 Tom Becker: for accuracy delta, what's acceptable? our product team says <1% drop is okay, >2% is maybe a regression. 02:26 Rafael Ortiz: okay we'll target <1% and flag the 2% line as a no-go. for cost targets, tell us the budget number and we'll reverse engineer the config. 02:35 Priya Nair: our internal target is $4000/month for inference today (for this feature) but we can go up to $10k/month if latency and accuracy are there. 02:44 Maya Chen: that's helpful — we'll produce a per-token cost model to show how each knob (batching, quantization, cache hit rate) affects your per-month bill. 02:52 Evan Liu: can you give a quick back-of-envelope? like int8 + caching savings vs fp16? 02:57 Rafael Ortiz: ballpark: int8 quantization alone tends to reduce compute cost by ~30–45% depending on kernels; effective prefix/KV caching (say 40–60% hit rate on repeated prefixes) can reduce token compute by another 20–50% on average for interactive. combined you can see 2–3x improvement in tokens-per-dollar in good cases. but, quantization may slightly increase latency variance — depends on hardware. 03:19 Priya Nair: we care about p95 especially — can't have tail latency spikes. 03:23 Rafael Ortiz: understood — part of the bench is to measure p95 under real traffic (we'll run a stress profile with realistic inter-arrival times). 03:31 Maya Chen: timeline-wise we recommend a 6-week POC: week 0 prep, week 1 bench kick-off + baseline runs, weeks 2–3 tuning configs (quant, cache, batching), week 4 customer validation on eval set, week 5 cost/ops review, week 6 signoff and next step conversation. 03:49 Tom Becker: that sounds good. do you need any infra from us? 03:52 Rafael Ortiz: for a hosted bench we just need sample prompts, an eval set, and your traffic histogram. if you want private/dedicated tests we'll coordinate a short window to spin up a Dedicated pool and provide access. 04:05 Janelle Park: if we do dedicated, we need to know about VPC peering and KMS — network ops will require a runbook. 04:12 Maya Chen: we'll include a network runbook and a checklist in the benchmark plan. 04:16 Priya Nair: another question — how do you model burst costs vs steady? our monthly spend is dominated by those nightly bursts and we need predictable caps. 04:24 Rafael Ortiz: two approaches: reserved capacity for nightly commit (Dedicated) to cap unit costs + hosted fallback for overflow; or smoothed autoscaling on hosted with throttles and queueing. we'll show both in the workbook with numeric examples: e.g., reserving X GPUs covers nightly 4k streams at Y cost; hosted overflow would be billed at standard rates but we can also model a prioritization policy to reduce cost. 04:46 Evan Liu: can you put some concrete numbers? like if we reserved 4xA10 equivalent for night ingest what would the monthly reserved cost look like? 04:54 Rafael Ortiz: we'll compute that in the pricing workbook — initial estimate: reserved pool covering the ingest might be in the $6k–$12k/month ballpark depending on utilization; hosted for overflow could add variable cost; exact numbers need the token distribution. 05:06 Priya Nair: ok fine, submit the workbook. we need the bench to answer: can we hit p95 300ms for interactive and keep monthly < $10k while staying within <1% accuracy loss. 05:18 Maya Chen: noted — we will define pass/fail gates tied to those three metrics and include a sensitivity analysis (cache hit from 20% to 80%, batch sizes, quant levels). 05:29 Tom Becker: what about tooling for ops — tracing, per-route cost breakdowns? 05:34 Anita Kapoor: Redwood Console will show per-route token breakdown, latency histograms, cost attribution, and we can integrate traces into your existing APM. we will include a short demo during the bench kickoff. 05:45 Janelle Park: and audit logs to SIEM? 05:47 Anita Kapoor: yes we can forward logs and show sample audit export in the trial. 05:52 Priya Nair: last thing — do you have prior customers with similar ingest patterns we can reference? any anonymized numbers? 05:59 Maya Chen: we can share anonymized case studies; one customer with heavy nightly ingestion saw a 2.1x tokens-per-dollar improvement after moving to a quantized + cache-first config. we'll include the high-level case study in the workbook. 06:12 Rafael Ortiz: quick note on benchmarks: we'll run three configs labeled A/B/C — A = fp16 baseline w/ batching tuned, B = int8 quantized, C = int8 + KV caching with warm prefix population. each run will report cost/1M tokens, p50/p95 latency, and accuracy delta. 06:33 Evan Liu: who runs the bench? your team or ours? 06:35 Maya Chen: Redwood will orchestrate the bench runs using your sample data; we'll ask for a point of contact from Silverpine to coordinate environments and approve traffic patterns — likely Janelle or Evan. 06:46 Priya Nair: okay Janelle/Evan I'll follow up internally and get those artifacts. 06:49 Maya Chen: perfect — next we'll send the detailed bench plan and the pricing workbook. any final questions? 06:54 Tom Becker: are there any gotchas with tokenization differences messing with our eval? 06:59 Rafael Ortiz: yes tokenizer mismatch can affect token counts; we'll standardize on the model tokenizer and also provide tokenized token counts in the workbook. if you have legacy accounting with different tokenization we'll show a conversion table. 07:10 Priya Nair: great, thanks everyone. 07:12 Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the bench kickoff. 07:16 (meeting ends)
notes_on_transcription: Occasional mislabels (Speaker 2 sometimes used for SE), minor word errors e.g., 'tokens-per-dollar' transcribed as 'tokens per dollar', timestamps approximate every ~30–90s. Some proper nouns like 'A10' GPU may be transcribed differently in the raw recording.
